annotation_description: With 2 mana available (Mountain + Blazemire Verge producing {R} and {B}), the player could have cast Moonshadow for {B} instead of Iron-Shield Elf for {1}{B}. Moonshadow is a 1/1 that grows as cards hit the graveyard, and casting it for {B} would have left the Mountain untapped, allowing the player to potentially hold up options or have mana available. More importantly, casting Moonshadow on turn 2 means it starts accumulating -1/-1 counter removals earlier — the Greasewrench Goblin already in the graveyard triggered one counter removal when it died. Iron-Shield Elf as a 3/1 is fragile and was already killed by Requiting Hex in the opponent's previous turn (the opponent has shown removal). Moonshadow for {B} is more mana-efficient and has better long-term upside, while Iron-Shield Elf could have been cast next turn alongside another spell.
